contrasting_investigations.what_changed_annotation: D1–D3 revise a mechanistic topology claim without erasing the electron-transfer role. C1–C2 constrain functional transfer between related membrane cores.
contrasting_investigations.not_resolved: Static topology does not reveal the complete access cycle. Genetic requirements do not independently prove every direct electron-transfer pair.

live_read_only_probe.origin: Our read-only deposited-record check; not an author experiment or independent structural solution.
live_read_only_probe.initial_question: Does the deposited MurJ structure contain lipid II that could locate the substrate-facing side directly?
live_read_only_probe.actual_followup_change: The lipid-containing entry prompted component-identity queries; absence of deposited lipid II shifted the next check to whether the paper’s substrate placement was modeled. The publisher preview labels Fig. 3 as a model of binding. I retained the intact-cell barrier controls as evidence for sided access, and did not use this deposit as a substrate-bound E. coli transport structure.
live_read_only_probe.inference_boundary: The deposition supports identity/content and a structural context. Ligand absence does not refute binding or transport. No coordinates, density, membrane orientation or docking were independently reanalyzed.

additional_source_correction.reconstructed_question_update: Relocation first raised the reaction-direction question. The later corrected strain comparison requires asking which accessible redox partner maintains that direction, rather than assigning it from compartment alone.
additional_source_correction.scope: Engineered variants; no claim of a natural export role.
